I am using the _nimble_ package instead of _jags_.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(nimble)

theme_set(ggthemes::theme_few())
```

```{r}
nchain <- 3
niter <- 5000
burnin <- 500
```


## Regression

$$ y \sim N_n( Xb, S^{-1}) $$ 

$$b_1, b_2 \sim N_p(b_0, s_b^{-1})$$

$$S \sim Gamma(s_1,s_2)$$


```{r}
load(here::here("data/Ex05.Part1.RData"))
df1 <- data.frame(
  x1 = x1,
  y = y
)
set.seed(1)
```

```{r}
model <- nimbleCode({
  b[1] ~ dnorm(b0, tau = sb)
  b[2] ~ dnorm(b0, tau = sb) ## Normal prior on regression params

  S ~ dgamma(s1, s2) ## prior precision

  for (i in 1:n) {
    mu[i] <- b[1] + b[2] * x[i] ## process model
    y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i], tau = S) ## data model
  }
})
```

```{r}
data <- list(
  x = df1$x1,
  y = df1$y
)

constants <- list(
  n = nrow(df1),
  b0 = 0,
  sb = 1 / 10000,
  s1 = 0.1,
  s2 = 0.1
)

ls_inits <- list()
for (i in 1:nchain) {
  ls_inits[[i]] <- list(b = rnorm(2, 0, 5), S = runif(1, 1 / 200, 1 / 20))
}
```

```{r}
Rmodel <- nimbleModel(
  code = model,
  constants = constants,
  data = data,
  inits = ls_inits
)

conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel)
conf$addMonitors(c("b", "S"))

Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)

samples <- runMCMC(Cmcmc,
  niter = niter,
  nburnin = 0,
  nchains = nchain,
  samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE
)

df_MCMC <- purrr::imap_dfr(samples, function(chain, ci) {
  as.data.frame(chain) |>
    mutate(n = row_number(), chain = factor(ci))
}) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(n, chain), names_to = "param", values_to = "value")
```

### Task 1 

-   Evaluate the MCMC chain for convergence. Include relevant diagnostics and plots. Determine and remove burn-in [A]

GBR statistic
```{r}
coda::gelman.diag(samples, autoburnin = F)$psrf
```

Traceplot
```{r}
df_MCMC |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_line(aes(x = n, y = value, color = chain), linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(. ~ param, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Discard 500 iterations as burn-in
```{r}
samples_burn <- window(samples, start = burnin + 1)

df_MCMC_burn <- purrr::imap_dfr(samples_burn, function(chain, ci) {
  as.data.frame(chain) |>
    mutate(n = row_number(), chain = factor(ci))
}) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(n, chain), names_to = "param", values_to = "value")

coda::gelman.diag(samples_burn, autoburnin = F)$psrf

df_MCMC_burn |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_line(aes(x = n, y = value, color = chain), linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(. ~ param, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

-   Report parameter summary table and plot marginal distributions [A]

```{r}
df_MCMC_burn |>
  group_by(param) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(value),
    lower = quantile(value, 0.025),
    upper = quantile(value, 0.975)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Parameter", "Median", "2.5%", "97.5%"),
    align     = "lrrr"
  )
```

```{r}
df_MCMC_burn |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_density(aes(x = value, color = chain)) +
  facet_wrap(. ~ param, scales = "free") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```


-   Describe and explain the parameter covariances that you observe in the pairs plot and parameter correlation matrix.[B]

```{r}
as.matrix(samples_burn) |> pairs()
as.matrix(samples_burn) |> cor()
```

-   Compare the summary statistics for the Bayesian regression model to those from the classical regression: `summary(lm(y ~ x1))`. This should include a comparison of the means and uncertainties of **all 3 model parameters** [A]

```{r}
reg <- lm(y ~ x1, data = df1)

summary(reg)$coefficients

1 / summary(reg)$sigma^2
```
## Multiple regression


$$ y \sim N_n( Xb, S^{-1}) $$ 

$$b_1, b_2, b_3, b_4 \sim N_p(b_0, s_b^{-1})$$

$$S \sim Gamma(s_1,s_2)$$


```{r}
load(here::here("data/Ex05.Part2.RData"))
df2 <- data.frame(
  x1 = x1,
  x2 = x2,
  y = y
)
set.seed(2)
```

### Task 2

- Show the JAGS and R code used. [A]

```{r}
model <- nimbleCode({
  b[1] ~ dnorm(b0, tau = sb)
  b[2] ~ dnorm(b0, tau = sb)
  b[3] ~ dnorm(b0, tau = sb)
  b[4] ~ dnorm(b0, tau = sb)

  S ~ dgamma(s1, s2) ## prior precision

  for (i in 1:n) {
    mu[i] <- b[1] + b[2] * x1[i] + b[3] * x2[i] + b[4] * x1[i] * x2[i] ## process model
    y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i], tau = S) ## data model
  }
})
```

```{r}
data <- list(
  x1 = df2$x1,
  x2 = df2$x2,
  y = df2$y
)

constants <- list(
  n = nrow(df1),
  b0 = 0,
  sb = 1 / 10000,
  s1 = 0.1,
  s2 = 0.1
)

ls_inits <- list()
for (i in 1:nchain) {
  ls_inits[[i]] <- list(b = rnorm(4, 0, 5), S = runif(1, 1 / 200, 1 / 20))
}
```

```{r}
Rmodel <- nimbleModel(
  code = model,
  constants = constants,
  data = data,
  inits = ls_inits
)

conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel)
conf$addMonitors(c("b", "S"))

Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)

samples <- runMCMC(Cmcmc,
  niter = niter,
  nburnin = 0,
  nchains = nchain,
  samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE
)

df_MCMC <- purrr::imap_dfr(samples, function(chain, ci) {
  as.data.frame(chain) |>
    mutate(n = row_number(), chain = factor(ci))
}) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(n, chain), names_to = "param", values_to = "value")
```
